I am 63 years old. I never went to school, not one day. I learned everything from my mother, starting when I was 15 years old, walking behind her in these same fields in Quzhou. Right now it is spring, and my winter wheat is already in the ground from last October. I have 8 mu of land and 11 mouths at home, but two of my grandsons work in Handan city and send money back. It is me, my husband, and my youngest son who do the farm work. We have our well, so when the sky turns dry we can pump water.

My land is split the same as last year. Six mu I use for wheat and then maize on the same ground — wheat in the winter half, maize in the summer half. One and a half mu I keep for cotton, because cotton brings cash at the end of the year when we need money for school fees and winter clothes. There is a half-mu corner plot by the road where I put mungbean. My daughter-in-law says it is good for the body, and it sells easy in the village.

For the wheat that is already growing: last October I put one big bag of compound fertilizer — 50 kg — into the ground when I planted. Last week I spread half a bag of urea because the wheat looked a little yellow after winter, and Auntie Li spread hers already so I did mine too. At jointing time I will spread another half bag of urea. That makes one bag of compound and one bag of urea for the whole season. I will water two more times — once now at green-up, and once when the heads start coming out. I already sprayed once for grass. I will spray one more time for the leaf-eating bugs. I hire the rotary tiller man to prepare the field, but I do the spraying myself with the backpack sprayer to save money. I expect about 900 jin per mu this year, same as last year.

After we cut the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize seed that very day — in summer you cannot wait even one day, the season is too short. I use 2.5 kg of seed per mu. I do not till again; I plant right into the wheat stubble. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer in the row at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I spread 30 kg of urea. I water twice — once right after planting if the rain doesn't come, and once when the tassels show. Three sprays: herbicide once, then bug medicine twice. Last year I got 1,000 jin per mu. I hope for the same, but the seed dealer raised prices, so I feel squeezed.

I am planting cotton this week on the 1.5 mu. Last month I paid the tractor man to plough that field deep with a moldboard plough because cotton roots hate hard ground. I plant 3 kg per mu of my own saved seed — cotton seed from the shop is too expensive, and my seed is fine. I put one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, then I will top-dress twice with about 15 kg of urea each time when the plants flower and when the bolls set. Three waterings. Cotton worms are my enemy — I spray four times, maybe five if I see holes in the bolls. I hope for 200 jin of seed cotton per mu. The cotton price was bad last year, but if I don't plant cotton, what cash do I have for the New Year?

For mungbean on the half-mu corner: I will plant in June after the first good rain. Two kg of my own saved seed. One small bag of compound fertilizer, 25 kg. Water once, maybe twice if it is very dry. One spray for aphids. It is an easy crop. I expect about 200 jin per mu, and I can pull it out before the autumn rains.

I do it this way because this is exactly what I did last year, and last year we did not go hungry. Fertilizer is expensive now — compound fertilizer is 150 yuan per bag, up from 130 last year — but I would rather put a little too much on the wheat than risk a bad harvest. If the wheat fails, we must borrow money from my nephew, and that is shame. If I waste some fertilizer, I just buy less new clothes. I watch my neighbors. When Old Zhang puts two bags of urea on his wheat, I put two bags. When Auntie Li sprays her cotton four times, I spray four times. We do not need books. We have eyes.
